overview: Markets: Rupee slid to a fresh 2-month low of 96.31/dollar amid global risk-off and foreign outflows.
Big story: The US moved thousands of troops toward the Middle East as Trump warned of fresh strikes on Iran.

items.headline: US moves troops, strike group toward Middle East over Iran
items.summary: The US is deploying roughly 9,000 troops and a naval strike group toward the Middle East after President Trump warned of possible new strikes on Iran following stalled peace talks. The build-up has already pushed oil prices higher and raises fears of a wider regional war.

items.headline: Russia's massive strike on Ukraine's power grid kills several
items.summary: Russia launched a combined drone-and-missile assault of nearly 190 projectiles on Ukraine's energy grid around Kyiv, triggering the capital's first emergency power cuts since spring. Ukraine's air force downed over 150 drones and several missiles, but the attack killed four people and knocked out infrastructure in five regions ahead of winter.

items.headline: Rupee slides to fresh two-month low against dollar
items.summary: The rupee fell 37 paise to close at 96.31 against the US dollar, its weakest level in over two months, as global bond yields surged and foreign investors sold Indian assets. Rising crude prices and broad risk aversion added to the pressure, a day after the currency had settled at 95.94.

items.headline: India's opposition plans nationwide protests over Election Commission row
items.summary: Opposition parties are preparing nationwide protests and renewing demands that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resign, accusing the BJP of manipulating a major revision of India's electoral rolls. The escalation deepens a dispute over voter-list integrity ahead of upcoming state elections.

items.headline: Wall Street rebounds as Treasury yields ease, chip stocks gain
items.summary: The Dow closed just above flat, the S&P 500 rose 0.2% and the Nasdaq edged higher as falling Treasury yields and gains in semiconductor stocks helped US markets recover from a choppy session. The rebound offers some relief after days of global risk-off selling tied to Middle East tensions.

items.headline: Israeli drone, settler attacks kill Palestinians in Gaza, West Bank
items.summary: An Israeli drone strike killed a Palestinian in Gaza while settlers killed another in the occupied West Bank, the latest violence despite a nearly year-old ceasefire. A Palestinian journalist was also among those killed this week, highlighting continued instability in the territory.

items.headline: Taipei indicts man over unregistered Chinese chipmaker office
items.summary: Prosecutors in Taipei indicted a man for allegedly operating an unregistered office for a Chinese semiconductor firm, seeking an 18-month prison sentence. The case underscores Taiwan's tightening scrutiny of Chinese business activity on the island amid rising cross-strait tensions.

items.headline: Milei courts investors in Paris as Argentina resets costs
items.summary: Argentina's President Javier Milei is courting investors in Paris even as pensions, rents and bills reset for citizens from October 1, reflecting the balancing act between attracting capital and managing austerity at home. The trip comes as Argentina seeks to sustain market confidence in its economic overhaul.

items.headline: Mexico finds relief after Hurricane Polo, unease over cartel sanctions
items.summary: Mexico is recovering after Hurricane Polo's remnants passed, even as new US sanctions on a Sinaloa Cartel network create fresh uncertainty alongside the country's ongoing export boom. The mixed picture reflects Mexico's balancing of disaster recovery with external economic pressure.

items.headline: Netanyahu: probe to clarify if FlyDubai co-pilot had Iran ties
items.summary: Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu said investigators would know within days whether a radicalized FlyDubai co-pilot involved in an aircraft diversion to Saudi Arabia had ties to Iran. He urged Israelis to stay on alert, as the incident adds to regional tension already stoked by the US military build-up.

items.headline: Bombay High Court orders takedown of AI deepfakes of actress
items.summary: The Bombay High Court ordered the takedown of AI-generated deepfakes and derogatory content misusing actress Samantha Ruth Prabhu's name, image and voice. The ruling adds to a growing body of Indian court orders addressing AI-enabled misuse of personal likeness.

items.headline: Delhi High Court eases travel curbs tied to pending PMLA cases
items.summary: The Delhi High Court quashed look-out circulars against individuals, holding that the mere pendency of a money-laundering investigation cannot indefinitely restrict a person's right to travel abroad. The ruling could ease curbs on businesspeople and professionals facing long-running ED probes.

items.headline: Allahabad High Court: police can't detain kin to force surrender
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court held that police cannot detain an innocent family member merely to pressure an accused person into surrendering. The ruling reinforces due-process protections against coercive policing tactics used in criminal investigations.

items.headline: Rajasthan High Court warns Jaipur's Walled City may lose UNESCO status
items.summary: The Rajasthan High Court warned that Jaipur's historic Walled City could lose its UNESCO World Heritage status unless authorities take corrective action by December, ordering a survey of illegal construction. Justice Pramil Kumar Mathur issued notices to ten state and local bodies over the civic lapses.

items.headline: Punjab and Haryana High Court flags 16-year delay in case listing
items.summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court sought a systemic fix after finding a case took 16 years just to be listed for hearing, spotlighting chronic delays in India's judicial process. The court's intervention adds pressure on the state's case-management system.

items.headline: Kerala High Court: wife sole owner of property bought with her funds
items.summary: The Kerala High Court ruled that a wife is the exclusive owner of a property purchased in both spouses' names when the funds came from her father, even though her husband was a joint title-holder. The judgment reinforces property rights based on the actual source of funds rather than title alone.

items.headline: Chhattisgarh High Court: new study-leave law can't apply retrospectively
items.summary: The Chhattisgarh High Court held that a newly passed law relaxing study-leave rules for government employees cannot be applied to past events, reaffirming that legislation operates prospectively unless stated otherwise. The ruling affects employees who had sought retrospective benefit under the amended rule.

items.headline: Mumbai's CSMT starts 75-day mega block for redevelopment
items.summary: Mumbai's Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus began a 75-day mega block from October 1 to carry out redevelopment work, likely disrupting suburban rail schedules. The extended block underscores the scale of infrastructure upgrades underway at one of India's busiest rail terminals.

items.headline: Commercial LPG cylinder prices hiked from October 1 in Maharashtra
items.summary: Commercial LPG cylinder prices rose from October 1, adding fresh inflation pressure for businesses and households just as the festive season begins. The hike comes amid broader cost-of-living concerns being felt across Indian states.

items.headline: Auto stocks lead Sensex-Nifty slide for fourth session
items.summary: The Sensex fell 571 points (0.79%) to 71,909 and the Nifty dropped nearly 199 points to 22,422, as auto stocks led the declines. Bajaj Auto, Maruti Suzuki and Shriram Finance were the top losers amid continued foreign investor selling and global risk aversion.

items.headline: Hero Motors stock hits new high, up 108% from listing low
items.summary: Shares of Hero Motors scaled a fresh high, rallying 108% from its listing-day low of Rs 80.50 on the BSE. The sharp rebound highlights renewed investor appetite for the auto-components maker since its stock market debut.

items.headline: MTNL stock jumps 17% on Rs 891-crore Powai land sale
items.summary: MTNL shares surged 17% after its board approved selling a Powai, Mumbai property worth Rs 891.53 crore to the income-tax department. The deal gives the debt-laden state-run telecom firm a fresh infusion of cash.

items.headline: Canara Bank advances cross Rs 12.63 trillion in quarterly update
items.summary: Canara Bank reported domestic advances rising to Rs 12.63 trillion and deposits to Rs 15.48 trillion in its provisional quarterly business update, pointing to continued strong credit growth. The numbers offer an early read on the banking sector ahead of formal Q2 earnings.

items.headline: Carlsberg India gets SEBI go-ahead for Rs 6,600-crore IPO
items.summary: Carlsberg India received SEBI's observations, effectively clearing the way, for a Rs 6,600 crore initial public offering. The listing would mark one of the larger consumer-sector IPOs in India's recent pipeline.

items.headline: SEBI keeps Inox Clean Energy's Rs 10,000-crore IPO papers in abeyance
items.summary: Capital markets regulator SEBI put Inox Clean Energy's draft offer documents for a proposed Rs 10,000 crore IPO on hold, delaying the renewable energy company's stock market debut. The move adds to a wave of large clean-energy IPOs awaiting regulatory clearance in India.

items.headline: SAT stays SEBI order barring Man Industries executives
items.summary: The Securities Appellate Tribunal granted Man Industries and three senior executives a stay on a SEBI order that had barred them from the markets, conditional on depositing half the penalty amount. The reprieve gives the company breathing room while it contests the regulator's findings.

items.headline: Phi Commerce names Rajesh Londhe as CEO for global push
items.summary: Payments platform Phi Commerce elevated Rajesh Londhe to chief executive as the company targets international expansion. The leadership change signals Phi Commerce's ambitions to grow beyond its domestic Indian payments business.

items.headline: Indian startups raise $2.9 billion in July-September quarter
items.summary: Indian startups raised $2.9 billion in equity funding during Q3 FY26, a slight dip from the previous quarter, with Bengaluru-based companies leading the pack. Mobility, AI and fintech drew the most investor attention, with AI startups alone pulling in over $635 million.

items.headline: Chile's copper output falls to 15-year low
items.summary: Chile's copper output fell 12.8% to its lowest level in 15 years, with prices holding near $14,417 a tonne. The decline in the world's top copper producer could tighten supply for EV and electronics manufacturers globally.

items.headline: Chile's unemployment hits 9.6%, highest since 2021
items.summary: Chile's jobless rate climbed to 9.6%, its highest since 2021, as a strike threat looms at the Centinela copper mine. Rising unemployment alongside falling copper output points to broader strain on Chile's commodity-dependent economy.

items.headline: Oil prices swing as Gulf flows partly ease Iran-driven risk
items.summary: Brent crude held near $104 a barrel, driven higher by Gulf geopolitical risk, even as reports that oil flows out of the Persian Gulf had partly recovered pulled WTI lower intraday. The volatility reflects markets weighing the US-Iran standoff against actual supply disruption.

items.headline: Satellite startup Satlyt raises $8 million to run AI in orbit
items.summary: Satlyt, founded by a former Google and SpaceX product manager, raised $8 million to develop software that runs AI workloads directly on satellites. The funding reflects growing investor interest in space-based computing infrastructure.

items.headline: Kevin Mandia's security startup Armadin raises $255.5 million
items.summary: Armadin, a new 'agent swarm' cybersecurity startup founded by former Mandiant CEO Kevin Mandia, raised $255.5 million at a $2.5 billion valuation. The large round underscores continued investor appetite for next-generation automated cyber-defense tools.

items.headline: Pentagon taps Elon Musk, Palmer Luckey on future tech strategy
items.summary: The Pentagon has brought in Elon Musk and Palmer Luckey to help shape decisions on the US military's next technology priorities. Their involvement signals deepening ties between Silicon Valley defense-tech entrepreneurs and US defense policy.

items.headline: DoorDash launches AI agent that orders food over text
items.summary: DoorDash rolled out an AI agent that customers can text to place food orders, aiming to simplify ordering outside its app. The launch is part of a broader industry push to embed conversational AI agents into everyday consumer services.

items.headline: Neko Health brings body-scan service to the US
items.summary: Neko Health, backed by Spotify billionaire Daniel Ek, launched its full-body scanning health service in the United States. The expansion marks the preventive-health startup's entry into the competitive American diagnostics market.

items.headline: PwC: enterprises underprepared for AI and quantum security threats
items.summary: A PwC survey found many enterprises are struggling to prepare their security defenses for emerging AI-driven and quantum-computing threats. The findings highlight a widening gap between the pace of AI adoption and organizations' cybersecurity readiness.

items.headline: SpaceX launches new four-astronaut crew to space station
items.summary: SpaceX launched a Crew Dragon carrying US, Canadian and Russian astronauts from Florida toward the International Space Station. The mission continues the steady cadence of crewed launches supporting ongoing ISS operations.

items.headline: WHO highlights Bhutan's success in eliminating rabies
items.summary: The World Health Organization cited Bhutan as proof that rabies elimination is achievable, pointing to the country's sustained vaccination and dog-population management programs. The example is being held up as a model for other countries battling the disease.

items.headline: WHO expands list of safe contraception options for women
items.summary: The World Health Organization broadened its recommended list of safe contraception methods, aiming to give women more choices backed by updated clinical evidence. The move is part of WHO's ongoing effort to improve reproductive health access globally.

items.headline: India edge Pakistan 4-3 in Asian Games hockey semifinal
items.summary: India beat Pakistan 4-3 in a dramatic Asian Games men's hockey semifinal, with Abhishek scoring the winning goal to send the defending champions into the gold-medal match. The win sets up another high-stakes India-Pakistan clash for gold.

items.headline: Nitesh Kumar wins Greco-Roman wrestling silver at Asian Games
items.summary: Nitesh Kumar won silver in Greco-Roman wrestling at the Asian Games, ending a 64-year wait for an Indian finalist in the discipline after defeating Mongolia's Gankhuyag Ganbaatar 9-0 en route to the final. The medal added to India's Day 12 haul of six medals.

items.headline: Teenager Anahati Singh wins squash silver at Asian Games
items.summary: Eighteen-year-old Anahati Singh won a silver medal in squash at the Asian Games, adding to India's growing medal tally at the Aichi-Nagoya Games. Her result continues a strong showing by young Indian athletes at this edition of the Games.

items.headline: Manchester City accused of 'sham' contracts inflating income by £830m
items.summary: Manchester City has been accused of arranging sham sponsorship contracts to inflate its income by £830 million, reigniting scrutiny of the club's finances under Premier League and UEFA financial fair play rules. The allegations could have significant implications for the club's regulatory standing.

items.headline: Arsenal blow two-goal lead in collapse against Paris FC
items.summary: Arsenal squandered a two-goal lead in a poor second-half collapse against Paris FC, raising fresh questions about the team's consistency in European competition. The result is a setback for Arsenal's continental campaign momentum.

items.headline: Gordon inspires England to win over Czech Republic
items.summary: England secured a much-needed win over the Czech Republic, with Anthony Gordon among the contributors in a result that eases pressure on the team following recent inconsistent form. The victory offers a confidence boost ahead of upcoming fixtures.
